children: While Anthropic's filing lays out big-picture risks to society from AI, including bioweapons and concentrated wealth, it identifies a more immediate threat to its own business: the growing anti-data-center movement in the U.S.
Because most Anthropic data centers are in the U.S., the company is vulnerable to threats including regulatory changes, moratoriums on the facilities and power failures.

"Opposition to data center development has also become more organized and coordinated across jurisdictions and our public profile may draw particular attention to projects associated with us," the company wrote. Anthropic said that it was expanding its international data-center network to reduce those risks and become less dependent on the U.S.
This item is part of a Wall Street Journal live coverage event. The full stream can be found by searching P/WSJL (WSJ Live Coverage).
